A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein kinase C is an important signaling molecule in the nucleus tract solitarii, the primary site of central respiratory control in the brainstem, that is involved in the modulation of the hypoxic ventilatory drive.
the NTS contains PKC, which is translocated and activated by acute hypoxia and mediates a significant portion of the hypoxic ventilatory drive in the adult rat.
the PKC signaling cascade in the commissural region of the NTS plays a pivotal role in the ventilatory response to acute hypoxia in the adult rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NTS is a critical site for the acute hypoxic chemoreflex, and PKC activation in this nucleus is essential for the expression of hypoxic ventilatory responses.
PKC activation in NTS mediates an essential component of the hypoxic ventilatory drive.
PKC activation in NTS is a necessary component of hypoxic ventilatory chemoreception.
